attribution.note: Marcus states this conclusion in his own voice and endorses it.

semantics.note: The surrounding discussion supplies OpenAI, ChatGPT, and mental-health risks as the subject of the historical assertion.

contract.note: The ordinary reading requires many disregarded warnings, without imposing a numerical threshold. Distinguishing disregard from imperfect responses and later remedies is fair; the meaning of quantity and disregard matters to the result.

evidence.note: Reporting supports disregarded concerns before the April release. Multiple witnesses to that decision do not establish many distinct mental-health warnings. Publication precedes the evaluation cutoff.
OpenAI's disclosure corroborates launching despite testers' concerns. Their nonspecific nature limits support for mental-health warnings; the later rollback does not erase the initial decision.
OpenAI reports subsequent mental-health safety improvements. This company disclosure does not establish whether earlier internal warnings received meaningful responses when decisions were made.

reviews.rationale: The packet substantiates an episode of proceeding despite internal concerns, but does not establish a substantial number or sustained pattern of distinct ignored ChatGPT mental-health warnings. Subsequent remedies and safety work do not disprove earlier disregard. Neither resolution condition is met.
